$comment: WHAT EACH ARTIFACT MUST CONTAIN, AND HOW EACH PACKAGE IS REACHED.
Written after a shipped outage: `ws-server.ts` reached the socket library
through a `createRequire()` shadow, which esbuild cannot see. The package
was never inlined, every released binary threw `Cannot find module 'ws'`,
and the catch handed over to a stub whose upgrade callback destroyed each
socket without writing a byte. Servers booted, printed a pairing code,
served /health and /webclient with 200s, and could not be paired to by
anything. Four weeks of binaries. No test could see it: every suite runs
from source, where node_modules is present and the require succeeds.
The two bundles have OPPOSITE requirements, which is the trap:
esm (dist/bin.js)  — a deferred require survives bundling as a runtime
lookup, so the package must EXIST ON DISK: external.
sea (dist/bin.cjs) — there is no node_modules at all, so everything must
be INLINED. Only a native .node can't be, and it
ships as a sidecar file beside the binary.
`scripts/build.mjs` verifies the emitted artifact against this file on
every build; `dependency-manifest.test.ts` verifies that this file, the
esbuild EXTERNAL list and package.json still agree.

ws.why: The WebSocket server. Was a createRequire-shadowed require until 2026-08-27; that is the outage above. Static import is what makes the SEA carry it.

imapflow.why: IMAP sync. Ambient `require` in imap-provider.ts, which esbuild CAN see and inline under CJS.

nodemailer.why: SMTP send. Must stay external in ESM: bundled there, esbuild rewrites its internal requires into a shim that throws. Bundled mailparser also deep-requires nodemailer/lib/addressparser at runtime.

mailparser.why: Static-import-only, so safe to bundle in both. Bundling it also removes its whole closure (iconv-lite, libmime, libqp, html-to-text) from the sidecar.

better-sqlite3-multiple-ciphers.why: The only irreducible one. `dlopen` needs a real file path, which no bundler can provide, so the addon ships beside the binary and open-database.ts loads it through createRequire(process.execPath). Its JS wrapper is inlined like everything else.

optional_unresolved.bufferutil: ws optional native frame masking — ws catches the missing module and uses its pure-JS path, identical behaviour, slightly slower.
optional_unresolved.utf-8-validate: ws optional native UTF-8 validation — same guarded fallback.

$optional_unresolved_rule: THE BAR IS 'STILL CORRECT WITHOUT IT', NOT 'DOES NOT CRASH'.
`ws` itself would have looked like a candidate for this list, and adding it
would have re-shipped the outage: its call site also 'handled' the missing
module — by falling back to a stub that silently killed every WebSocket.
Before adding an entry, ask what the fallback DOES, not whether one exists.
